source.citation: Ross PJ (2011), Numerical Solution of the Continuity Equation for Soil Water Flow Using Precomputed Steady-State Fluxes, Vadose Zone Journal 10:760-766
source.relationship: uses the Ross 2003 continuity-equation time discretization but replaces online approximate Darcian face evaluation by lookup of accurately precomputed steady-state face fluxes

source_bound_algorithm.face_flux: bilinear interpolation in a two-end-state table q(v_upper,v_lower)
source_bound_algorithm.flux_derivatives: obtained from the same table interpolation and used in a first-order Taylor expansion over the trial time step
source_bound_algorithm.column_step: one tridiagonal linear solve for state increments, not a global nonlinear iteration
source_bound_algorithm.retry: if state change is unacceptable, reduce the time step; source states that fluxes and derivatives need not be recalculated for that retry
source_bound_algorithm.mass: finite-volume discretization is stated to conserve mass to computational error
source_bound_algorithm.heterogeneous_face: a table can represent a path composed of two materials; accurate composite entries may be generated offline with an equal-flux/steady-Darcy boundary-value solve
source_bound_algorithm.mfp_role: Kirchhoff/matric-flux-potential transform is used to accelerate and regularize offline generation of accurate steady-state flux tables, not required in production lookup
source_bound_algorithm.hysteresis: not supported by the source method because flux is assumed to be a unique function of endpoint state

cost_model.runtime_per_internal_step: O(N_cells) table lookups plus O(N_cells) tridiagonal linear solve
cost_model.offline_table_generation: potentially expensive iterative ODE/root solution but reusable immutable template/material-geometry data
cost_model.source_operation_estimate: Ross 2011 estimated about 112 weighted operation units per grid cell per step versus 374 for the Ross 2003 implementation and 179 per HYDRUS iteration
cost_model.source_runtime_observation: in three reported tests the table method was 1.5 to 3.2 times faster than Ross 2006 and execution time per step remained approximately constant across differing hydraulic property complexity
cost_model.multiswap_fit: promising if material/geometry/path-class cardinality and table memory remain bounded and shared

hydraulics: van Genuchten retention with tested conductivity forms
reported_table_memory_examples: about 58 KB for six tables in tests 1-2
72 KB for eight tables in test 3
12 KB for two tables in test 4
source_test_evidence.reported_table_density_sensitivity: doubling the table interval changed drainage materially in test 3b, while halving changed little
source_test_evidence.important_limit: accurate steady-state face flux does not eliminate transient spatial-discretization error; sharp infiltration fronts inside coarse cells remain a stated source of error

SWAP5_assessment.reason: bounded linear-time runtime, shared immutable face-class data, exact finite-volume mass structure, generic endpoint hydraulics and no global nonlinear iteration align closely with SWAP5 invariants
critical_open_gates: reconstruct exact Ross 2003/2011 time-discrete linear system including saturated-unsaturated transitions
prove SWAP5 accepted-step mass closure with sinks, drainage, surface and groundwater exchange
replace any historical disk/file ownership with kernel-external immutable parameter preparation
qualify SWAP hydraulic catalog including near-saturation discontinuities and inverse theta-head behavior
bound path-class/table cardinality for MultiSWAP templates
qualify generic timestep/retry controller and maximum internal substep count
derive imposed-bottom-head and imposed-bottom-flux semantics plus response tangent
quantify coarse-cell transient error against FullRichards for infiltration, drying, capillary rise, clay and moving water table

relationship_to_layeredmfp.commonality: both exploit high-quality local steady Darcian/MFP face information and immutable shared lookup structures
relationship_to_layeredmfp.difference: Ross 2011 retains a depth-discretized finite-volume continuity system with a global tridiagonal linear update, whereas LayeredMFP is a reduced-order layer-storage model with bounded local interface solves
relationship_to_layeredmfp.research_implication: do not duplicate face-oracle science; reuse or cross-qualify the F-LMFP06-09 Darcian face machinery as a reference for RossFast table generation where contracts permit
